To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the chloroplast translation machinery can insert the bacterial membrane protein leader pepidase (Lp) into thylakoids, and that Lp insertion is cotranslational and requires SecA.

a bacterial membrane protein, leader peptidases (Lep), is efficiently translated in a chloroplast translation system and can be inserted into thylaoid membranes with the positive-inside topology, that insertion is stimulated by the proton gradient, is SecA-dependent, and is cotranslational.

the chloroplast translation machinery can be used to study the mechanisms of protein targeting and membrane insertion and that the insertion of the bacterial leader peptidases into the chloroplast thylakoid and the E. colicytoplasmic membrane is similar, supporting a functional homology of these membrane systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of the import and insertion of chloroplastic membrane proteins.
the mechanisms of protein targeting and insertion into the thylakoide membrane.
the mechanism of protein insertion into thylakoids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Lep is inserted into the chloroplast thylakoid in a manner that resembles the bacterial system, and this is in line with the current view of a bacterial-type protein insertion pathway into the thylackoid membrane.
the insertion of Lep in chloroplasts is a process similar to that of E. coli.
the thylakoids of chloroplasts have a membrane protein insertion system that is functionally similar to that of bacteria and the endoplasmatic reticulum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the targeting and insertion mechanisms of the chloroplast translation machinery are highly similar to those of the E. coli and the endoplasmatic reticulum systems, and the chloroplast translation apparatus is able to insert a bacterial protein into the thylacoid membrane.
the chloroplast translation machinery and the thylakoidal membrane are capable to insert Lep in a manner similar to the E. coli system.
a chloroplast translation system is able to translate and insert a bacterial thylakoid-targeted membrane protein in an E. coli-like manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thylakoids are a good system in which to study protein targeting and insertion, as they are a relatively simple membrane and the system is well characterized.
the thylakoids of chloroplasts are able to insert proteins into their membranes by a mechanism that is very similar to that in the cytoplasmic (inner) membranes of E. coli.
the insertion of Lep in chloroplasts is a cotranslional process and that the ribosome interacts with the thylakoids during this process.
